| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `definition` | `PluginDefinition<TServices>` | Yes | Plugin metadata and a synchronous route-registration callback. Duplicate method/path pairs are rejected. |

### Returns

`DefinedPlugin`

Frozen metadata and route array; version defaults to 0.0.0, and entitlement/schema dependencies are copied.

### Type parameters

- `TServices`: Host services exposed to handlers; defaults to a record of unknown values.

### Remarks

Runs routes synchronously during definition. Does not mount handlers or connect database/storage; the host supplies scoped capabilities after admission.

### Errors and rejections

Error for invalid ID, entitlement, route or duplicate method/path; route-registration callback errors propagate.

### Example

```typescript
import { definePlugin } from "@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/define-plugin";
const plugin = definePlugin({ id: "notes", routes(router) { router.get("/status", () => ({ ready: true })); } });
console.log(plugin.routeDefinitions.length); // 1
```


<a id="api-deliverWithRetry"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `deliverWithRetry`

POST a signed JSON webhook with bounded exponential retry attempts.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/webhook`, `@alneas/eaos-core/webhook/delivery`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function deliverWithRetry(options: DeliveryOptions): Promise<DeliveryResult>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `DeliveryOptions` | Yes | Destination, secret and payload; maxRetries is the total attempt count (default 3), backoffMs is the base delay (default 1000), and custom headers override generated headers. |

### Returns

`Promise<DeliveryResult>`

Success with one-based attempt/status, or failure data after attempts are exhausted; HTTP and fetch errors are returned rather than thrown.

### Remarks

Requires fetch and node:crypto. All non-2xx responses/fetch errors are retried; there is no cancellation or request timeout. The timestamp/signature are reused across attempts; the receiver must handle duplicate effects safely. No options validation is performed.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects if initial JSON serialization or signature construction fails before delivery.

### Example

```typescript
import { deliverWithRetry } from "@alneas/eaos-core/webhook/delivery";
const destination = process.env.WEBHOOK_TEST_URL;
const secret = process.env.WEBHOOK_TEST_SECRET;
if (!destination || !secret) throw new Error("Configure a test receiver and its shared secret");
const result = await deliverWithRetry({ url: destination, secret, payload: { event: "demo", timestamp: Date.now(), data: { message: "hello" } } });
console.log(result);
```


<a id="api-DeliveryOptions"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `DeliveryOptions`

Destination, signing secret, payload, attempt count and optional header overrides.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/webhook`, `@alneas/eaos-core/webhook/delivery`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface DeliveryOptions {
    url: string;
    secret: string;
    payload: WebhookPayload;
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoffMs?: number;
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | Yes | Target/observed HTTP(S) location; adapter/host authorization must restrict navigation and delivery. |
| `secret` | `string` | Yes | Shared or one-time secret value; keep it out of persistence/logs except through host-approved secret storage. |

<a id="api-DomainEventBus"></a>

## [CLASS] `DomainEventBus`

Maintain in-memory subscriptions and dispatch payloads synchronously.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/index`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/event-bus`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class DomainEventBus {
    publish<T>(eventName: string, payload: T): void;
    subscribe<T>(eventName: string, handler: EventHandler<T>): void;
    unsubscribe<T>(eventName: string, handler: EventHandler<T>): void;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| — | — | — | No call parameters. |

### Returns

`DomainEventBus`

### Remarks

No persistence, buffering, retries or tenant filtering is supplied. Use one bus per host/request scope; listeners receive the original payload reference.

### Public members

#### `publish`

Invoke current listeners synchronously in Set iteration order.

Parameters:

- `eventName`: Exact subscription key.
- `payload`: Payload passed by reference to each listener.

Returns: No value; synchronous dispatch has finished, but listener Promises are not awaited.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Payload type agreed by publisher and listener; no runtime check occurs.

### Remarks

Rejected listener Promises are not handled by the bus; listeners must handle asynchronous failures.

### Errors and rejections

Synchronous listener errors propagate and stop dispatch to later listeners.

Example:

```typescript
import { DomainEventBus } from "@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/event-bus";
const bus = new DomainEventBus();
bus.publish("note.created", { id: "note-1" });
```


#### `subscribe`

Add a listener to an event key.

Parameters:

- `eventName`: Exact event key.
- `handler`: Listener invoked during publish with the original payload. Repeated registration of the same function is deduplicated.

Returns: No value; the listener is registered.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Payload type agreed by publisher and listener; no runtime check occurs.

### Remarks

Caller owns unsubscription; payload typing is a caller contract rather than runtime validation.

Example:

```typescript
import { DomainEventBus } from "@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/event-bus";
const bus = new DomainEventBus();
const handler = (payload: { id: string }) => { console.log(payload.id); };
bus.subscribe("note.created", handler);
bus.unsubscribe("note.created", handler);
```


#### `unsubscribe`

Remove a listener by its function identity.

Parameters:

- `eventName`: Subscription key.
- `handler`: The same function reference passed to subscribe.

Returns: No value; absent subscriptions are ignored.

### Type parameters

- `T`: Payload type agreed by publisher and listener; no runtime check occurs.

Example:

```typescript
import { DomainEventBus } from "@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/event-bus";
const bus = new DomainEventBus();
const handler = (payload: { id: string }) => { console.log(payload.id); };
bus.subscribe("note.created", handler);
bus.unsubscribe("note.created", handler);
```



### Example

```typescript
import { DomainEventBus } from "@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/event-bus";
const bus = new DomainEventBus();
const handler = (payload: { id: string }) => { console.log(payload.id); };
bus.subscribe("note.created", handler);
bus.publish("note.created", { id: "note-1" });
bus.unsubscribe("note.created", handler);
```

<a id="api-DurableAuditTrail"></a>

## [CLASS] `DurableAuditTrail`

Serialize audit events through a host sink and advance the local hash only after acceptance.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class DurableAuditTrail {
    constructor(sink: AuditSink<PlatformAuditEvent>, clock?: () => Date);
    append(input: PlatformAuditEventInput): Promise<PlatformAuditEvent>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sink` | `AuditSink<PlatformAuditEvent>` | Yes | Host durable append capability; awaited before advancing this instance hash. |
| `clock` | `() => Date` | No | Optional timestamp callback invoked for each append; defaults to current Date. |

### Returns

`DurableAuditTrail`

### Remarks

Requires node:crypto. Each instance starts at zero-hash genesis and has no persisted-head recovery API; host lifecycle must avoid presenting independent instances as one continuous chain. A rejected sink may have partially committed; deduplication/reconciliation belong to the host.

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `append`

Clone and append one hash-linked event after earlier queued appends settle.

Parameters:

- `input`: Audit scope/action/outcome; copied before generated UUID, timestamp and previousHash are added.

Returns: The appended event after sink acceptance; the sink receives a separate structured clone.

### Remarks

A failure does not stop subsequent queued appends. No cancellation or retry is implemented; a rejected host write can have an uncertain durable outcome.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects on cloning/serialization/date failures or propagated sink rejection.

Example:

```typescript
import { DurableAuditTrail } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security";
import type { AuditSink } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/audit-sink";
import type { PlatformAuditEvent } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security";
async function appendHostEvent(sink: AuditSink<PlatformAuditEvent>) {
 const trail = new DurableAuditTrail(sink);
 return trail.append({ tenantId: "tenant-demo", userId: "user-demo", action: "notes.preview", outcome: "success" });
}
```



### Example

```typescript
import { DurableAuditTrail } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security";
import type { AuditSink } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/audit-sink";
import type { PlatformAuditEvent } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security";

 const trail = new DurableAuditTrail(sink);
 return trail.append({ tenantId: "tenant-demo", userId: "user-demo", action: "notes.preview", outcome: "success" });
}
```

<a id="api-eligibilityRequirementsSchema"></a>

## [CONSTANT] `eligibilityRequirementsSchema`

Closed JSON Schema limiting course and qualification requirement arrays to 50 entries each.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/index`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/eligibility`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare const eligibilityRequirementsSchema: {
    readonly type: "object";
    readonly additionalProperties: false;
    readonly required: readonly [
        "courses",
        "qualifications"
    ];
    readonly properties: {
        readonly courses: {
            readonly type: "array";
            readonly maxItems: 50;
            readonly items: {
                readonly type: "object";
                readonly additionalProperties: false;
                readonly required: readonly [
                    "namespace",
                    "id",
                    "version",
                    "contentHash"
                ];
                readonly properties: {
                    readonly namespace: {
                        readonly type: "string";
                        readonly pattern: "^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$";
                    };
                    readonly id: {
                        readonly type: "string";
                        readonly pattern: "^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,80}$";
                    };
                    readonly version: {
                        readonly type: "string";
                        readonly pattern: "^\\d{1,6}\\.\\d{1,6}\\.\\d{1,6}$";
                    };
                    readonly contentHash: {
                        readonly type: "string";
                        readonly pattern: "^[a-f0-9]{64}$";
                    };
                };
            };
        };
        readonly qualifications: {
            readonly type: "array";
            readonly maxItems: 50;
            readonly items: {
                readonly type: "object";
                readonly additionalProperties: false;
                readonly required: readonly [
                    "issuer",
                    "id"
                ];
                readonly properties: {
                    readonly issuer: {
                        readonly type: "string";
                        readonly minLength: 1;
                        readonly maxLength: 100;
                    };
                    readonly id: {
                        readonly type: "string";
                        readonly minLength: 1;
                        readonly maxLength: 100;
                    };
                };
            };
        };
    };
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| — | — | — | No call parameters. |

### Returns

`Declared constant value.`

### See also

[eligibilityRequirementsSchema](#api-eligibilityRequirementsSchema)

### Example

```typescript
import { eligibilityRequirementsSchema } from "@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/eligibility";
console.log(eligibilityRequirementsSchema.properties.courses.maxItems); // 50
```


### Parameters

| `riskLevel` | `AIRiskLevel` | Yes | Operational risk tier (1: Read-only, 2: Routine draft, 3: Critical mutation). |

### Returns

`{     allowed: boolean;     humanConfirmationRequired: boolean;     reason?: string; }`

### Public members

#### `options.isDirectMutation`

Whether the requested operation directly changes persisted state.


#### `options.hasHumanConfirmation`

Whether the host has obtained human confirmation for this operation.


#### `result.allowed`

Whether this advisory risk check permits the requested execution path.


#### `result.humanConfirmationRequired`

Whether the host must require a human action before proceeding.


#### `result.reason`

Optional explanation for a blocked execution path.



### Example

```typescript
import { evaluateAIRiskPolicy } from '@alneas/eaos-core/ai/governance';

```

## [FUNCTION] `evaluatePluginEntitlement`

Pure preview shared by server and UI. A UI decision is never a server capability.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk`, `@alneas/eaos-core/entitlements`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/index`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function evaluatePluginEntitlement(pluginId: string, rule: PluginEntitlement, tenantId: string, entitlement: TenantEntitlements | null, now?: Date): EntitlementDecision;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pluginId` | `string` | Yes | Valid plugin identifier used as a quota key when no addon ID is set. |
| `rule` | `PluginEntitlement` | Yes | Plugin policy validated before evaluation. |
| `tenantId` | `string` | Yes | Tenant whose access is being previewed. |
| `entitlement` | `TenantEntitlements \| null` | Yes | Trusted tenant snapshot, or null when absent; any supplied tenant ID must match. |
| `now` | `Date` | No | Evaluation time; defaults to a newly constructed current Date. |

### Returns

`EntitlementDecision`

Allowed with optional quota, or a denial carrying status 402/404 and reason. This helper does not consume quota or compare usage.

### Remarks

Pure preview only. The host must enforce admission and quotas; an allowed browser result is not a server capability.

### Errors and rejections

Error for malformed policies/snapshots, invalid time or scope, or a mismatched tenant.

### Example

```typescript
import { evaluatePluginEntitlement } from "@alneas/eaos-core/entitlements";

```

### Signature

```typescript

```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `condition` | `WorkflowCondition` | Yes | Validated condition; all/any/not recurse, dotted paths use own properties and equality uses Object.is. |

### Returns

`boolean`

Whether the condition matches. Missing paths fail positive comparisons but satisfy not_equals/not_in and falsy.

### Remarks

Does not validate the condition first or execute expression strings. Validate untrusted definitions with validateWorkflowDefinition.

### Example

```typescript
import { evaluateWorkflowCondition } from "@alneas/eaos-core/workflow-definition";
console.log(evaluateWorkflowCondition({ path: "amount", operator: "greater_than", value: 10 }, { amount: 12 })); // true
```

<a id="api-ExecutionSandbox"></a>

## [CLASS] `ExecutionSandbox`

Dispatch a legacy execution request to simulation or an optional Tauri IPC bridge.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/execution-sandbox`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class ExecutionSandbox {
    executeCode(request: SandboxExecutionRequest, options?: {
        mode?: ExecutionBridgeMode;
        cliType?: ExecutionCliType;
        userContext?: {
            userId: string;
            roles: string[];
        };
    }): Promise<{
        requiresHumanApproval: boolean;
        approvalTicketId?: string;
        result?: SandboxExecutionResult;
    }>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| — | — | — | No call parameters. |

### Returns

`ExecutionSandbox`

### Remarks

docker_cloud is a simulation and does not run a container or code. tauri_local_cli invokes window.__TAURI__.invoke when available and otherwise returns simulated success. The current gate uses a fixed tenant key and checks requireHumanApproval withoutenforcing allowed; this helper must not serve as a production authorization or isolation boundary.

### Public members

#### `executeCode`

Return a review ticket or dispatch through the selected legacy execution bridge.

Parameters:

- `request`: Script metadata; docker_cloud reports a simulation, while Tauri receives code as the CLI prompt. timeoutMs/environmentVariables are not enforced here.
- `options`: Mode defaults to docker_cloud, cliType to antigravity and roles to agent; userId is not used by the implementation.

Returns: An approval-required result with an unpersisted ticket ID, or reported/simulated execution data. Tauri IPC errors are converted to exitCode 1.

### Remarks

No cancellation, real cloud sandbox, durable ticket, timeout or replay prevention is implemented. A returned success may be simulated. Hosts must use an admitted, scoped execution adapter for real effects.

Example:

```typescript
import { ExecutionSandbox } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/execution-sandbox";
const sandbox = new ExecutionSandbox();
console.log(await sandbox.executeCode({ taskId: "task-1", agentId: "agent-1", language: "javascript", code: "1 + 1" }));
```


#### `executeCode.requiresHumanApproval`

Whether this bridge response requires a separate host approval workflow.


#### `executeCode.approvalTicketId`

Unpersisted legacy review-ticket identity; the host must not treat it as approval evidence.


#### `executeCode.result`

Optional reported/simulated execution details; absence accompanies a review-required response.


#### `executeCode.options.mode`

Selected operation/storage/execution variant; the owning discriminated union determines applicable fields.


#### `executeCode.options.cliType`

Optional desktop CLI bridge identifier; defaults to antigravity in executeCode.


#### `executeCode.options.userContext`

Optional desktop bridge user/roles metadata; current implementation reads roles only.


#### `executeCode.options.userContext.userId`

User identity within the tenant supplied by the trusted host.


#### `executeCode.options.userContext.roles`

Role claims supplied by the host after identity verification.



### Example

```typescript
import { ExecutionSandbox } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/execution-sandbox";
const sandbox = new ExecutionSandbox();
console.log(await sandbox.executeCode({ taskId: "task-1", agentId: "agent-1", language: "javascript", code: "1 + 1" }));
```

<a id="api-generateJournalDraftFromDocument"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `generateJournalDraftFromDocument`

Domain-agnostic pipeline helper that extracts line items from parsed document tables
and generates an AI-to-UI draft (Level 2) with balanced double-entry lines.

Hosts supply account mappings and context through an injected resolver.
Unit-price-only columns are excluded; the helper requires a line-total amount column.
Preview totals retain numeric minor units; hosts supply currency formatting.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/index`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/journal-draft`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/construction-journal-pipeline`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function generateJournalDraftFromDocument<TContext = unknown>(request: GenerateJournalDraftRequest<TContext>): {
    draftEntry: Omit<ImmutableLedgerEntry, 'id'>;
    uiDraft: CoreAiDraft;
};
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `request` | `GenerateJournalDraftRequest<TContext>` | Yes | Tenant, period, parsed source, actor and injected account mapping for the candidate. |

### Returns

`{     draftEntry: Omit<ImmutableLedgerEntry, 'id'>;     uiDraft: CoreAiDraft; }`

Balanced DRAFT entry data and a corresponding reviewable UI proposal.

### Type parameters

- `TContext`: Host context type passed unchanged to the injected account resolver.

### Errors and rejections

If no positive whole minor-unit line amounts are found, balance validation fails, or the host mapping resolver throws.

### Public members

#### `result.draftEntry`

Unposted balanced entry candidate without a persisted identifier.


#### `result.uiDraft`

Reviewable UI proposal containing candidate values; no persistence is performed.



### Example

```typescript
import { generateJournalDraftFromDocument } from '@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/journal-draft';
const result = generateJournalDraftFromDocument({ tenantId: 'tenant-demo', periodId: 'period-1', createdBy: 'actor-1', parsedDoc: { name: 'source.pdf', markdown: '2026-10-24', tables: [{ headers: ['項目', '金額'], rows: [['Service', '100']] }] }, mapping: { debitAccountId: 'account-debit', creditAccountId: 'account-credit' } });
console.log(result.draftEntry.status); // DRAFT
```


| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `timestamp` | `string` | Yes | Timestamp text, conventionally Unix epoch milliseconds; signed verbatim without validation. |
| `body` | `string` | Yes | Exact serialized body; whitespace changes alter the signature. |
| `secret` | `string` | Yes | Shared HMAC secret. |

### Returns

`string`

Lowercase hexadecimal signature over timestamp + dot + body.

### Remarks

Requires node:crypto. Receivers must independently enforce timestamp freshness and replay protection.

### Example

```typescript

```

<a id="api-GraphProjectionAdapter"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `GraphProjectionAdapter`

Host-owned projection update/rebuild and optional cursor port.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/workflow-runtime`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface GraphProjectionAdapter {
    apply(event: WorkflowEventEnvelope): Promise<void>;
    rebuild(input: {
        tenantId: string;
        sourceRevision: number;
        snapshot: unknown;
    }): Promise<void>;
    getCursor?(tenantId: string): Promise<GraphProjectionCursor | null>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apply` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Apply one workflow event to a host graph projection. |
| `rebuild` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Rebuild a tenant projection from a host source snapshot. |
| `getCursor` | `Promise<GraphProjectionCursor \| null>` | No | Read optional host projector progress for a tenant. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

[createWorkflowEvent](#api-createWorkflowEvent)

### Public members

#### `apply`

Apply one workflow event to a host graph projection.

Parameters:

- `event`: Tenant-scoped source event; host should deduplicate its identity/revision as appropriate.

Returns: No value; host projection apply has completed.

### Remarks

Host owns isolation, durable cursor updates, ordering and idempotency. Core supplies no projector transaction.

### Errors and rejections

Host projection failures reject; partial updates depend on host atomicity.

Example:

```typescript
import type { GraphProjectionAdapter } from "@alneas/eaos-core/workflow-runtime";
async function applyHostEvent(adapter: GraphProjectionAdapter, event: Parameters<GraphProjectionAdapter["apply"]>[0]) { await adapter.apply(event); }
```


#### `rebuild`

Rebuild a tenant projection from a host source snapshot.

Parameters:

- `input`: Verified tenant, source revision and complete snapshot interpreted by the host.

Returns: No value; host rebuild has completed.

### Remarks

Host defines atomic replacement, concurrent event handling, resource limits and recovery; this method can replace persisted read-model data.

### Errors and rejections

Host rebuild failures reject and may leave a partial/old projection depending on host atomicity.

Example:

```typescript
import type { GraphProjectionAdapter } from "@alneas/eaos-core/workflow-runtime";
async function rebuildHost(adapter: GraphProjectionAdapter, snapshot: unknown) { await adapter.rebuild({ tenantId: "tenant-demo", sourceRevision: 1, snapshot }); }
```


#### `rebuild.input.tenantId`

Verified tenant boundary for the record or operation; host authorization must establish this scope.


#### `rebuild.input.sourceRevision`

Optional nonnegative safe-integer source revision represented by the graph result.


#### `rebuild.input.snapshot`

Host-provided source snapshot used for projection rebuild; the adapter owns atomic replacement and isolation.


#### `getCursor`

Read optional host projector progress for a tenant.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Verified tenant whose cursor is requested.

Returns: Cursor or null when no progress is available.

### Remarks

Optional capability; absent lookup does not establish projector health.

### Errors and rejections

Host cursor-read failures reject.

Example:

```typescript
import type { GraphProjectionAdapter } from "@alneas/eaos-core/workflow-runtime";
async function inspectCursor(adapter: GraphProjectionAdapter) {
 if (!adapter.getCursor) throw new Error("Host cursor lookup is unavailable");
 return adapter.getCursor("tenant-demo");
}
```



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

<a id="api-hasActiveConsent"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `hasActiveConsent`

Find a matching consent that has started, remains unrevoked and has not expired.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function hasActiveConsent(records: readonly ConsentRecord[], requirement: {
    tenantId: string;
    userId: string;
    purpose: string;
    version?: string;
    now?: Date;
}): boolean;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `records` | `readonly ConsentRecord[]` | Yes | Host-supplied consent records; any qualifying match is sufficient. |
| `requirement` | `{     tenantId: string;     userId: string;     purpose: string;     version?: string;     now?: Date; }` | Yes | Exact tenant/user/purpose and optional version; omitted now uses current Date and absent/falsy version accepts any version. |

### Returns

`boolean`

Whether at least one active record matches.

### Remarks

Does not persist consent or establish that records came from a trusted source.

### Public members

#### `requirement.tenantId`

Exact trusted tenant identity to match against consent records.


#### `requirement.userId`

Exact authenticated user identity whose grant must match within the tenant.


#### `requirement.purpose`

Exact consent purpose identifier; a grant for another purpose does not satisfy this requirement.


#### `requirement.version`

Optional exact consent revision; omission or an empty string accepts any recorded version.


#### `requirement.now`

Optional evaluation clock for grant-start/expiry checks; omission uses current Date. A matching record must be granted at or before this instant and unrevoked/unexpired.



### Example

```typescript
import { hasActiveConsent } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security";
const records = [{ tenantId: "tenant-demo", userId: "user-demo", purpose: "summarization", version: "1", grantedAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z" }];
const requirement = { tenantId: "tenant-demo", userId: "user-demo", purpose: "summarization", version: "1", now: new Date("2026-10-19T00:00:00Z") };
console.log(hasActiveConsent(records, requirement)); // true
```

Read-only host probe with an identifier, criticality and optional deadline.

```typescript

    id: string;

```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Yes | Unique lowercase probe identity, at most 128 characters, used for result correlation. |
| `critical` | `boolean` | No | Whether failure makes readiness not_ready; defaults to true. False failures only degrade readiness. |
| `timeoutMs` | `number` | No | Optional execution deadline in milliseconds; enforcement belongs to the API/runtime consuming this metadata. |
| `run` | `() => boolean \| Promise<boolean>` | Yes | Run a read-only host readiness probe when aggregation starts. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

[runReadinessChecks](#api-runReadinessChecks)

### Public members

#### `id`

Unique lowercase probe identity, at most 128 characters, used for result correlation.


#### `critical`

Whether failure makes readiness not_ready; defaults to true. False failures only degrade readiness.


#### `timeoutMs`

Optional execution deadline in milliseconds; enforcement belongs to the API/runtime consuming this metadata.


#### `run`

Run a read-only host readiness probe when aggregation starts.

Returns: True only when the checked condition is healthy, directly or asynchronously; false/throws/rejections become failed probe results.

### Remarks

Called concurrently with other probes. Timeout stops waiting without cancelling this callback; the host owns resource cleanup.

Example:

```typescript
import type { HealthCheck } from "@alneas/eaos-core/health";
const configuration = { initialized: true };
const check: HealthCheck = { id: "configuration", run: () => configuration.initialized };
console.log(await check.run());
```

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core/platform/config`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface IngressHostRoute {
    host: string;
    target: 'backend' | 'frontend' | {
        host: string;
        port: number;
        resolution?: 'docker' | 'system';
    };
    proxy?: {
        readTimeoutSeconds?: number;
        sendTimeoutSeconds?: number;
        buffering?: boolean;
    };
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `host` | `string` | Yes | Exact public DNS name; inherits the app scheme and listener port. |
| `target` | `'backend' \| 'frontend' \| {     host: string;     port: number;     resolution?: 'docker' \| 'system'; }` | Yes | Managed services follow their resolved name/port; custom HTTP services stay host-owned. |
| `proxy` | `{     readTimeoutSeconds?: number;     sendTimeoutSeconds?: number;     buffering?: boolean; }` | No | Per-route ingress settings; default read/send timeouts are 180 seconds and buffering is false. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

[resolvePlatformConfig](#api-resolvePlatformConfig)

### Public members

#### `host`

Exact public DNS name; inherits the app scheme and listener port.


#### `target`

Managed services follow their resolved name/port; custom HTTP services stay host-owned.


#### `target.host`

Exact DNS route or HTTP upstream name; managed route hosts must remain under baseDomain.


#### `target.port`

Required integer TCP port from 1 to 65535 for the host-owned custom HTTP upstream.


#### `target.resolution`

Upstream hostname resolution strategy, docker by default for resolved host routes.


#### `proxy`

Per-route ingress settings; default read/send timeouts are 180 seconds and buffering is false.


#### `proxy.readTimeoutSeconds`

Ingress upstream read timeout in seconds; defaults to 180.


#### `proxy.sendTimeoutSeconds`

Ingress upstream send timeout in seconds; defaults to 180.


#### `proxy.buffering`

Ingress proxy buffering selection; defaults to false.

<a id="api-InstinctEngine"></a>

## [CLASS] `InstinctEngine`

Keep session-derived heuristics locally and optionally read a host vector index.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/instinct-engine`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class InstinctEngine {
    constructor(vectorAdapter?: VectorSearchAdapter | undefined);
    extractInstinctsFromSession(params: {
        tenantId: string;
        domain: string;
        history: Array<{
            role: string;
            content: string;
        }>;
        success: boolean;
        extractFn?: (history: Array<{
            role: string;
            content: string;
        }>) => Promise<{
            pattern: string;
            heuristic: string;
            confidence: number;
        }>;
    }): Promise<AgentInstinct | null>;
    findRelevantInstincts(options: {
        tenantId: string;
        domain: string;
        queryVector?: number[];
        topK?: number;
    }): Promise<AgentInstinct[]>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vectorAdapter` | `VectorSearchAdapter \| undefined` | No | Trusted host search adapter; omitted means local lookup only. |

### Returns

`InstinctEngine`

### Remarks

Extraction stores only process-local references and does not embed or index them. Vector search results are mapped from host metadata without an additional tenant-result validator; the adapter must enforce tenant scope. Search failures log a warning and fall back to local filtering.

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `extractInstinctsFromSession`

Extract or synthesize one heuristic from a successful multi-turn session.

Parameters:

- `params`: Tenant/domain and history; returns null for unsuccessful sessions or fewer than two turns. Optional extractFn receives history and resolves pattern/heuristic/confidence; failures log a warning and use built-in defaults.

Returns: A newly stored local instinct reference, or null. Default confidence is 0.85 with one success and zero failures.

### Remarks

No embedding/index write, output validation or durable persistence occurs. The caller must handle sensitive trajectory content and validate extractor output.

Example:

```typescript
import { InstinctEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/instinct-engine";
const engine = new InstinctEngine();
console.log(await engine.extractInstinctsFromSession({ tenantId: "tenant-demo", domain: "notes", success: true, history: [{ role: "user", content: "Preview notes" }, { role: "assistant", content: "No changes" }] }));
```


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.tenantId`

Verified tenant boundary for the record or operation; host authorization must establish this scope.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.domain`

Classification key copied to the extracted local heuristic.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.history`

Session turns supplied for lifecycle/extraction; sensitive content handling remains host-owned.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.history[].role`

Host conversation-speaker label associated with this history turn.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.history[].content`

Loaded skill instructions, model response text or proposed file content; treat external text as untrusted input.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.success`

Reported completion flag; inspect status/receipt and reconcile any uncertain side effects before retrying.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.extractFn`

Extract a proposed heuristic from successful session history.

Parameters:

- `history`: Original session turns passed by reference after success and minimum-length checks.

Returns: Proposed pattern, heuristic and confidence; the engine uses them without domain/range validation.

### Remarks

Host owns provider access and sensitive-history handling; this callback does not write a vector index.

### Errors and rejections

Callback rejections are caught/logged by extraction, which retains its default heuristic.

### See also

[InstinctEngine.extractInstinctsFromSession](#api-InstinctEngine)

Example:

```typescript
import type { InstinctEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/instinct-engine";
async function extractWithHost(params: Parameters<InstinctEngine["extractInstinctsFromSession"]>[0]) {
 if (!params.extractFn) throw new Error("Configure a host extractor");
 return params.extractFn(params.history);
}
```


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.extractFn.history[].role`

Host conversation-speaker label associated with this history turn.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.extractFn.history[].content`

Loaded skill instructions, model response text or proposed file content; treat external text as untrusted input.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.extractFn.result.pattern`

Host-extracted session pattern; the engine accepts it without shape/range validation.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.extractFn.result.heuristic`

Reusable suggested handling text extracted or synthesized from a session.


#### `extractInstinctsFromSession.params.extractFn.result.confidence`

Reported confidence ratio, conventionally from zero to one; validate at the consuming boundary.


#### `findRelevantInstincts`

Read vector-index matches when configured, otherwise filter local heuristics.

Parameters:

- `options`: Tenant/domain and optional query vector/topK. topK defaults to 5; vector queries use indexId ai-instincts and do not include a domain filter.

Returns: Mapped provider results, or original local references filtered by exact tenant/domain in insertion order.

### Remarks

Provider errors are logged and fall back locally. The adapter is trusted for result tenant scope and score/metadata validity; no cancellation/retry is supplied.

Example:

```typescript
import { InstinctEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/instinct-engine";
const engine = new InstinctEngine();
console.log(await engine.findRelevantInstincts({ tenantId: "tenant-demo", domain: "notes", topK: 5 }));
```


#### `findRelevantInstincts.options.tenantId`

Verified tenant boundary for the record or operation; host authorization must establish this scope.


#### `findRelevantInstincts.options.domain`

Exact domain filter for local fallback; vector search does not send this as a filter.


#### `findRelevantInstincts.options.queryVector`

Nonempty finite numeric embedding; the host checks its dimension against the selected index.


#### `findRelevantInstincts.options.topK`

Requested maximum result count; vector request validation permits integers from 1 to 10000.



### Example

```typescript
import { InstinctEngine } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/instinct-engine";
const engine = new InstinctEngine();
console.log(await engine.findRelevantInstincts({ tenantId: "tenant-demo", domain: "notes" })); // []
```

## [FUNCTION] `invertJournalLines`

Inverts the debit/credit sides of balanced journal lines without creating or posting an entry.
Pure mathematical operation compatible with any accounting plugin.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/index`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/immutable-ledger`.


| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lines` | `readonly ImmutableLedgerLine[]` | Yes | Original journal lines. |

### Returns

`ImmutableLedgerLine[]`

Reversing lines with 'D' and 'C' swapped.

### Errors and rejections

If input lines fail the balance, count, account, side or minor-unit amount checks.

### Example

```typescript
import { invertJournalLines } from '@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/immutable-ledger';
const inverted = invertJournalLines([{ accountId: 'account-debit', side: 'D', amount: 100 }, { accountId: 'account-credit', side: 'C', amount: 100 }]); // No entry is posted.
```

<a id="api-issueApiKey"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `issueApiKey`

Generate a secret once; only the digest is suitable for persistence.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function issueApiKey(input: {
    tenantId: string;
    userId: string;
    scopes: readonly string[];
    id?: string;
    now?: Date;
    expiresAt?: string | null;
}): IssuedApiKey;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | `{     tenantId: string;     userId: string;     scopes: readonly string[];     id?: string;     now?: Date;     expiresAt?: string \| null; }` | Yes | Tenant/user IDs and nonempty scopes; optional ID defaults to randomUUID, now to current Date, and expiry must be absent/null or strictly after now. |

### Returns

`IssuedApiKey`

The secret and record. Persist only record; return the secret to its owner through a protected channel.

### Remarks

Requires node:crypto. Does not persist or authorize key issuance; the host must protect the secret and enforce tenant/key policy.

### Errors and rejections

Error for blank identity/scopes or nonfuture expiry; date/crypto failures propagate.

### Public members

#### `input.tenantId`

Nonblank host-verified tenant identity bound to the generated key record; this function does not authorize key issuance.


#### `input.userId`

Nonblank verified key owner identity copied into the persistence record.


#### `input.scopes`

Nonempty exact permission-scope names; every entry must be nonblank. Verification later matches a requested scope exactly.


#### `input.id`

Optional host key-record identity; omission generates a random UUID, without checking external uniqueness.


#### `input.now`

Optional issuance clock used for createdAt and expiry comparison; omission uses a new current Date.


#### `input.expiresAt`

Optional parseable absolute expiry strictly after now; null or omission means no expiry is recorded.



### Example

```typescript
import { issueApiKey } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/platform-security";
const issued = issueApiKey({ tenantId: "tenant-demo", userId: "user-demo", scopes: ["notes:read"] });
console.log(issued.record.prefix);
```

## [FUNCTION] `legacyNumberToDecimal`

Explicit adapter for existing numeric feeds, preserving their displayed decimal value.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/index`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/decimal-values`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function legacyNumberToDecimal(value: number): string;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number` | Yes | Finite JavaScript number; any precision already lost in the number cannot be recovered. |

### Returns

`string`

### Errors and rejections

### Example

```typescript
import { legacyNumberToDecimal } from "@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/decimal-values";
```

<a id="api-McpCacheManager"></a>

## [CLASS] `McpCacheManager`

Store process-local tool cache entries and manually incremented tenant call counts.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core/agent/cache-manager`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class McpCacheManager {
    setTenantQuota(tenantId: string, config: QuotaConfig): void;
    checkQuota(tenantId: string): {
        allowed: boolean;
        reason?: string;
    };
    incrementQuota(tenantId: string): void;
    getCache(tenantId: string, toolName: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): unknown | undefined;
    setCache(tenantId: string, toolName: string, args: Record<string, unknown>, data: unknown, ttlSeconds?: number): void;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| — | — | — | No call parameters. |

### Returns

`McpCacheManager`

### Remarks

No persistence, eviction timer or cross-process coordination. Cache keys use JSON.stringify argument order. Daily counts reset by UTC date; the monthly count is retained across date changes and has no implemented month reset. Quota checks do not increment usage; zero limits are treated as absent.

### Public members

#### `setTenantQuota`

Replace the quota configuration stored for a tenant.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Tenant quota lookup key.
- `config`: Daily/monthly call limits stored by reference; omitted or zero limits are not enforced.

Returns: No value; limits have been set.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpCacheManager } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agent/cache-manager";
const cache = new McpCacheManager();
cache.setTenantQuota("tenant-demo", { maxCallsPerDay: 100 });
```


#### `checkQuota`

Check configured call counts without reserving or consuming quota.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Tenant quota key; tenants without limits are allowed.

Returns: Allowed or denied with a reason; checking may initialize/reset the UTC daily counter.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpCacheManager } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agent/cache-manager";
const cache = new McpCacheManager();
console.log(cache.checkQuota("tenant-demo").allowed); // true
```


#### `checkQuota.allowed`

Admission/check decision; consumers must inspect it before using the associated result or performing an effect.


#### `checkQuota.reason`

Human-readable explanation of the decision or requested action.


#### `incrementQuota`

Increment both call counters for a tenant.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Tenant whose usage increases; works even without a configured limit.

Returns: No value; daily/monthly counters have increased.

### Remarks

Resets daily count on a new UTC date, retaining monthly count. No atomic admission reservation occurs with checkQuota.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpCacheManager } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agent/cache-manager";
const cache = new McpCacheManager();
cache.incrementQuota("tenant-demo");
```


#### `getCache`

Read a tool result and lazily remove an expired entry.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Tenant key.
- `toolName`: Exact tool name.
- `args`: Arguments serialized in insertion order to form the cache key.

Returns: The original cached data reference, or undefined on miss/expiry; cached undefined is indistinguishable from a miss.

### Errors and rejections

JSON serialization errors for unsupported argument values, including cycles and bigint.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpCacheManager } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agent/cache-manager";
const cache = new McpCacheManager();
console.log(cache.getCache("tenant-demo", "notes.list", {}));
```


#### `setCache`

Replace a cached tool result with an expiration time.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Tenant key.
- `toolName`: Exact tool name.
- `args`: Arguments serialized in insertion order to form the cache key.
- `data`: Result stored by reference.
- `ttlSeconds`: Lifetime in seconds relative to Date.now; defaults to 60 and is not validated.

Returns: No value; the entry has been stored.

### Errors and rejections

JSON serialization errors for unsupported argument values, including cycles and bigint.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpCacheManager } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agent/cache-manager";
const cache = new McpCacheManager();
cache.setCache("tenant-demo", "notes.list", {}, ["note-1"]);
```



### Example

```typescript
import { McpCacheManager } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agent/cache-manager";
const cache = new McpCacheManager();
cache.setCache("tenant-demo", "notes.list", {}, ["note-1"], 60);
console.log(cache.getCache("tenant-demo", "notes.list", {}));
```

<a id="api-McpGatekeeper"></a>

## [CLASS] `McpGatekeeper`

Evaluate local tool policies and record bounded hash-linked audit entries.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class McpGatekeeper {
    constructor(dbAdapter?: DatabaseAdapter | undefined, auditSink?: GatekeeperAuditSink | undefined, options?: GatekeeperOptions);
    registerPolicy(toolName: string, policy: ExtendedGatekeeperPolicy): void;
    validateCall(params: {
        toolName: string;
        userRoles: string[];
        tenantId: string;
        traceId?: string;
    }): {
        allowed: boolean;
        reason?: string;
        requireHumanApproval: boolean;
        riskLevel: RiskLevel;
        approvalLevel: ApprovalLevel;
    };
    logCall(entry: Omit<GatekeeperAuditEntry, 'id' | 'timestamp' | 'hash' | 'previousHash' | 'approvalLevel'> & {
        approvalLevel?: ApprovalLevel;
    }): GatekeeperAuditEntry;
    logCallDurably(entry: Omit<GatekeeperAuditEntry, 'id' | 'timestamp' | 'hash' | 'previousHash' | 'approvalLevel'> & {
        approvalLevel?: ApprovalLevel;
    }): Promise<GatekeeperAuditEntry>;
    getAuditDeliveryFailures(): readonly {
        entryId: string;
        error: string;
    }[];
    getAuditLogs(tenantId?: string): GatekeeperAuditEntry[];
    getTraceLogs(traceId: string): GatekeeperAuditEntry[];
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dbAdapter` | `DatabaseAdapter \| undefined` | No | Optional host database adapter used for task_audit_logs insertion; the connection must support execute for that insertion path. |
| `auditSink` | `GatekeeperAuditSink \| undefined` | No | Optional durable append sink; when both destinations exist both are awaited by durable logging. |
| `options` | `GatekeeperOptions` | No | Optional logging policy; requireDurableAudit defaults to false and disables legacy logCall when true. |

### Returns

`McpGatekeeper`

### Remarks

Requires node:crypto. Missing policies default to allowed/low/L1_AUTO; this is not a fail-closed authorization system. Validation checks roles, not tenant admission, consent, entitlements or evidence. Local audit view is capped at 500 entries; durable delivery is host-supplied. Avoid mixing legacy and durable logging concurrently when a single ordered chain is required.

### Constructor contract

### Public members

#### `registerPolicy`

Store or replace a tool policy by reference.

Parameters:

- `toolName`: Exact tool/skill identity used by validateCall.
- `policy`: Role, risk and review policy; later external mutation changes future evaluations.

Returns: No value; the policy has been replaced.

### Errors and rejections

Error when the declared AI risk tier is not 1, 2 or 3.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper();
gatekeeper.registerPolicy("notes.preview", { riskLevel: "low", requiredRole: "member" });
```


#### `validateCall`

Evaluate role admission and derive risk/approval metadata without executing a tool.

Parameters:

- `params`: Tool name, verified user roles and tenant/trace metadata; current evaluation uses toolName and roles only.

Returns: Allowed/denied decision plus risk, required review flag and approval level. No policy means low/L1_AUTO allowed; role arrays mean any match and admin/SUPER_ADMIN bypass role restrictions.

### Remarks

No audit is automatically recorded. A caller must honor allowed and requireHumanApproval, and separately enforce tenant, entitlement and evidence policy.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper();
console.log(gatekeeper.validateCall({ toolName: "notes.preview", userRoles: ["member"], tenantId: "tenant-demo" }).allowed); // true
```


#### `validateCall.allowed`

Admission/check decision; consumers must inspect it before using the associated result or performing an effect.


#### `validateCall.reason`

Human-readable explanation of the decision or requested action.


#### `validateCall.requireHumanApproval`

Whether execution must wait for an explicit host approval workflow.


#### `validateCall.riskLevel`

Declared operation risk used to determine review requirements; it does not itself grant authorization.


#### `validateCall.approvalLevel`

Required organizational review category; a level declaration is not proof of approval.


#### `validateCall.params.toolName`

Registered tool identity used to resolve host execution policy.


#### `validateCall.params.userRoles`

Verified host role claims passed to gatekeeper/runtime evaluation.


#### `validateCall.params.tenantId`

Verified tenant boundary for the record or operation; host authorization must establish this scope.


#### `validateCall.params.traceId`

Trace correlation identity propagated through host execution and audit paths.


#### `logCall`

Append a local audit entry and start best-effort configured persistence.

Parameters:

- `entry`: Audit scope/outcome; ID, timestamp and hash links are generated, and approval level is derived from risk when omitted.

Returns: The local audit entry reference, before any asynchronous persistence has completed.

### Remarks

Persistence failures are retained in a bounded 100-entry diagnostic list. Completion does not prove durable storage; use logCallDurably when persistence is required.

### Errors and rejections

Error when requireDurableAudit is enabled, or JSON hashing fails.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper();
console.log(gatekeeper.logCall({ toolName: "notes.preview", userId: "user-demo", tenantId: "tenant-demo", status: "ALLOWED", riskLevel: "low" }).hash);
```


#### `logCall.entry.approvalLevel`

Required organizational review category; a level declaration is not proof of approval.


#### `logCallDurably`

Serialize audit appends and add the local entry only after configured destinations accept it.

Parameters:

- `entry`: Audit scope/outcome; generated identity/timestamp/hash and default approval level follow logCall semantics.

Returns: The appended entry after all configured deliveries resolve.

### Remarks

Multiple sinks are not one transaction: one may accept before another rejects. The local chain hash is rolled back on failure, but accepted external writes are not undone; hosts must reconcile partial outcomes before retrying.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects without a durable destination, on hashing errors, or when a configured database/sink write rejects.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
import type { GatekeeperAuditSink } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
async function appendHostAudit(sink: GatekeeperAuditSink) {
 const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper(undefined, sink, { requireDurableAudit: true });
 return gatekeeper.logCallDurably({ toolName: "notes.preview", userId: "user-demo", tenantId: "tenant-demo", status: "ALLOWED", riskLevel: "low" });
}
```


#### `logCallDurably.entry.approvalLevel`

Required organizational review category; a level declaration is not proof of approval.


#### `getAuditDeliveryFailures`

Copy the bounded legacy persistence-failure diagnostics.

Returns: New failure objects in a new array, up to the latest 100 legacy failures.

### Remarks

Local diagnostics are not a substitute for durable host audit storage.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper();
console.log(gatekeeper.getAuditDeliveryFailures()); // []
```


#### `getAuditDeliveryFailures[].entryId`

Identity of the audit entry whose delivery failed.


#### `getAuditDeliveryFailures[].error`

Optional human-readable failure detail; absence does not independently establish success.


#### `getAuditLogs`

Read the bounded local audit view, optionally filtering by tenant.

Parameters:

- `tenantId`: Optional exact tenant key; omission or a falsy value exposes the full local array.

Returns: A filtered array when tenantId is truthy, otherwise the internal mutable array; entries remain original references.

### Remarks

Local diagnostics are not a substitute for durable host audit storage.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper();
console.log(gatekeeper.getAuditLogs("tenant-demo")); // []
```


#### `getTraceLogs`

Filter local audit entries by exact trace identity.

Parameters:

- `traceId`: Trace correlation key.

Returns: New array containing original matching entry references.

### Remarks

Local diagnostics are not a substitute for durable host audit storage.

Example:

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper();
console.log(gatekeeper.getTraceLogs("trace-1")); // []
```



### Example

```typescript
import { McpGatekeeper } from "@alneas/eaos-core/security/gatekeeper";
const gatekeeper = new McpGatekeeper();
console.log(gatekeeper.validateCall({ toolName: "notes.preview", userRoles: ["member"], tenantId: "tenant-demo" }));
```

<a id="api-ModelRoutingGateway"></a>

## [CLASS] `ModelRoutingGateway`

Apply built-in prompt heuristics and choose from a fixed model catalog.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/agentic`, `@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/model-routing-gateway`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class ModelRoutingGateway {
    sanitizePrompt(prompt: string): SanitizationResult;
    selectModel(tier: ModelTier, sensitivityLevel: DataSensitivityLevel): ModelRoutingConfig;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| — | — | — | No call parameters. |

### Returns

`ModelRoutingGateway`

### Remarks

This is a heuristic helper, not comprehensive PII detection or verified provider policy. Model metadata is static; no provider is called.

### Public members

#### `sanitizePrompt`

Mask recognized phone/email patterns and classify prompt text heuristically.

Parameters:

- `prompt`: Text inspected for phone/email patterns and selected Japanese confidentiality/internal markers.

Returns: Original/sanitized text, detected types, replacement map and recommended tier.

### Remarks

Retains the original prompt and sensitive values in the result; caller must protect it. Pattern detection is incomplete and does not establish a privacy guarantee.

Example:

```typescript
import { ModelRoutingGateway } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/model-routing-gateway";
const gateway = new ModelRoutingGateway();
console.log(gateway.sanitizePrompt("Contact demo@example.com").sensitivityLevel); // level3_strict
```


#### `selectModel`

Select a built-in model by sensitivity and requested tier.

Parameters:

- `tier`: Preferred tier for nonstrict data.
- `sensitivityLevel`: Strict data selects the first MLX local model regardless of tier; other levels filter by tier and allowedSensitivity.

Returns: The original mutable model configuration; when no ordinary match exists the first catalog entry is returned.

### Remarks

Does not enforce live provider no-training agreements or authorization; fallback can disregard the requested tier.

Example:

```typescript
import { ModelRoutingGateway } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/model-routing-gateway";
const gateway = new ModelRoutingGateway();
console.log(gateway.selectModel("tier2_edge_local", "level3_strict").provider);
```



### Example

```typescript
import { ModelRoutingGateway } from "@alneas/eaos-core/agentic/model-routing-gateway";
const gateway = new ModelRoutingGateway();
const result = gateway.sanitizePrompt("Contact demo@example.com");
console.log(result.sanitizedPrompt);
```

<a id="api-OutboxDispatcher"></a>

## [CLASS] `OutboxDispatcher`

Claim and settle one bounded batch through host-owned storage and topic handlers.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare class OutboxDispatcher {
    constructor(options: OutboxDispatcherOptions);
    runOnce(): Promise<OutboxDispatchResult>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | `OutboxDispatcherOptions` | Yes | Required store/handlers and optional admission wrapper/clock/retry settings; defaults are 20 records, 5 attempts, 1000 ms base, 60000 ms cap and multiplier 2. |

### Returns

`OutboxDispatcher`

### Remarks

No timers, cancellation or automatic looping. Hosts own scheduling, atomic claims/claim tokens, tenant admission and idempotent effects. Records are handled sequentially; handler success followed by settlement failure can cause a retry of an already-completed effect.

### Constructor contract

### Remarks

Constructing the dispatcher performs no claim, handler call or scheduling. Retry settings are validated when retryDelayMs is used.

### Errors and rejections

Error for missing store/handlers or batchSize outside integer range 1–100.

### Public members

#### `runOnce`

Claim due events and execute/settle each one sequentially.

Returns: Counts of claimed, published, rescheduled and terminally failed records; empty batches return zero counts.

### Remarks

Unknown topic errors are terminal; other errors retry unless OutboxDispatchError says otherwise or attempts are exhausted. Concurrent runOnce safety depends on atomic host claims; no exactly-once guarantee is provided.

### Errors and rejections

Rejects on store claim/markFailed errors, invalid retry calculations or clock failures. Handler/admission/markPublished failures normally become failed/rescheduled records.

Example:

```typescript
import { OutboxDispatcher } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
import type { OutboxDispatcherOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
async function dispatchHostBatch(options: OutboxDispatcherOptions) {
 const dispatcher = new OutboxDispatcher(options);
 return dispatcher.runOnce();
}
```



### Example

```typescript
import { OutboxDispatcher } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
import type { OutboxDispatcherOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
async function dispatchHostBatch(options: OutboxDispatcherOptions) {
 return new OutboxDispatcher(options).runOnce();
}
```


<a id="api-OutboxDispatcherOptions"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `OutboxDispatcherOptions`

Host persistence, handlers, scheduling clock and optional admission wrapper for a worker pass.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface OutboxDispatcherOptions {
    store: OutboxStore;
    handlers: Record<string, (event: Readonly<OutboxEvent>) => Promise<void>>;
    now?: () => Date;
    retryPolicy?: Partial<OutboxRetryPolicy>;
    batchSize?: number;
    execute?: (event: Readonly<OutboxEvent>, handler: () => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `store` | `OutboxStore` | Yes | Transactional host outbox port; claiming and settlement must enforce claim ownership and tenant scope. |
| `handlers` | `Record<string, (event: Readonly<OutboxEvent>) => Promise<void>>` | Yes | Map exact event topics to asynchronous effect handlers. |
| `now` | `() => Date` | No | Provide the worker clock used for claiming and settlement timestamps. |
| `retryPolicy` | `Partial<OutboxRetryPolicy>` | No | Optional retry overrides; dispatcher defaults to 5 attempts, 1000 ms base, 60000 ms maximum and multiplier 2. |
| `batchSize` | `number` | No | Maximum claim size for one pass, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20. |
| `execute` | `(event: Readonly<OutboxEvent>, handler: () => Promise<void>) => Promise<void>` | No | Optionally enforce live host admission immediately before the handler side effect. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

[createOutboxEvent](#api-createOutboxEvent)

### Public members

#### `store`

Transactional host outbox port; claiming and settlement must enforce claim ownership and tenant scope.


#### `handlers`

Map exact event topics to asynchronous effect handlers.

### Remarks

Each callback receives a cloned readonly event and resolves without a value after its effect completes. Rejections normally schedule retries, so handlers must be replay-safe; use OutboxDispatchError with retryable false for terminal failures.

### See also

[OutboxDispatcher.runOnce](#api-OutboxDispatcher)


#### `now`

Provide the worker clock used for claiming and settlement timestamps.

Returns: Current valid Date; omission uses a new Date for each clock call.

### See also

[OutboxDispatcher.runOnce](#api-OutboxDispatcher)

Example:

```typescript
import type { OutboxDispatcherOptions } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
function readHostClock(options: OutboxDispatcherOptions) {
 return options.now?.() ?? new Date();
}
```


#### `retryPolicy`

Optional retry overrides; dispatcher defaults to 5 attempts, 1000 ms base, 60000 ms maximum and multiplier 2.


#### `batchSize`

Maximum claim size for one pass, from 1 to 100; defaults to 20.


#### `execute`

Optionally enforce live host admission immediately before the handler side effect.

Parameters:

- `event`: Claimed readonly event whose tenant/plugin lifecycle must still permit execution.
- `handler`: Deferred callback invoking the registered effect handler; await it only after admission succeeds.

Returns: No value; completion means the wrapper and any invoked handler have completed.

### Remarks

Omission calls handler directly. Host owns authorization, replay safety and partial-outcome reconciliation.

### Errors and rejections

Wrapper/handler failures enter dispatcher retry/failure settlement.

### See also

[OutboxDispatcher.runOnce](#api-OutboxDispatcher)

Example:

```typescript
import type { OutboxDispatcherOptions, OutboxEvent } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
async function invokeHostWrapper(options: OutboxDispatcherOptions, event: OutboxEvent) {
 const handler = options.handlers[event.topic];
 if (!handler || !options.execute) throw new Error("Configure a handler and live host admission wrapper");
 await options.execute(event, () => handler(event));
}
```



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

## [INTERFACE] `OutboxStore`

Transactional host storage port for claiming and settling outbox records.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface OutboxStore {
    claim(now: Date, limit: number): Promise<readonly OutboxEvent[]>;
    markPublished(id: string, claimToken: string, publishedAt: Date): Promise<void>;
    markFailed(id: string, claimToken: string, error: string, retryAt: Date | null): Promise<void>;
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `claim` | `Promise<readonly OutboxEvent[]>` | Yes | Atomically claim a bounded set of due records for one host worker. |
| `markPublished` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Settle a claimed event after its handler completes. |
| `markFailed` | `Promise<void>` | Yes | Settle a failed claim with either a retry schedule or terminal state. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

[createOutboxEvent](#api-createOutboxEvent)

### Public members

#### `claim`

Atomically claim a bounded set of due records for one host worker.

Parameters:

- `now`: Host claim time used to determine due work.
- `limit`: Maximum records requested; dispatcher supplies its validated batch size.

Returns: Claimed records with host-owned claim/attempt metadata, possibly empty.

### Remarks

Host owns transaction/CAS, leases, tenant isolation and claim tokens. Concurrent workers must not claim the same live record.

### Errors and rejections

Host claim failures reject the Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { OutboxStore } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
async function claimHostEvents(store: OutboxStore) { return store.claim(new Date(), 20); }
```


#### `markPublished`

Settle a claimed event after its handler completes.

Parameters:

- `id`: Claimed event identity.
- `claimToken`: Exact live claim ownership token.
- `publishedAt`: Host publication completion timestamp.

Returns: No value; the host settlement has completed.

### Remarks

Host must enforce claim ownership and durable settlement. A rejection after the handler effect does not prove the effect failed.

### Errors and rejections

Host settlement failures reject the Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { OutboxStore } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
async function settleHostEvent(store: OutboxStore, id: string, claimToken: string) { await store.markPublished(id, claimToken, new Date()); }
```


#### `markFailed`

Settle a failed claim with either a retry schedule or terminal state.

Parameters:

- `id`: Claimed event identity.
- `claimToken`: Exact live claim ownership token.
- `error`: Sanitized failure text; dispatcher truncates Error messages to 1000 characters.
- `retryAt`: Future due time for a retry, or null for terminal failure.

Returns: No value; the host failure/retry settlement has completed.

### Remarks

Host must enforce claim ownership and atomically release/reschedule the claim; Core does not implement storage.

### Errors and rejections

Host settlement failures reject the Promise.

Example:

```typescript
import type { OutboxStore } from "@alneas/eaos-core/events/outbox";
async function failHostEvent(store: OutboxStore, id: string, claimToken: string) { await store.markFailed(id, claimToken, "Temporary failure", new Date(Date.now() + 1000)); }
```

<a id="api-parseWorkflowAgentProposal"></a>

## [FUNCTION] `parseWorkflowAgentProposal`

Parse the bounded JSON envelope emitted by a host runtime. Domain-specific
validation of `output` remains in the plugin workflow.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/workflow-contracts`.

### Signature

```typescript
declare function parseWorkflowAgentProposal<TOutput = unknown>(raw: unknown): WorkflowAgentProposal<TOutput>;
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `raw` | `unknown` | Yes | JSON text or an object with schemaVersion 1.0, nonempty summary, evidence/actions arrays and a valid risk level. |

### Returns

`WorkflowAgentProposal<TOutput>`

A structured clone of the normalized proposal; output is carried through without domain-schema validation.

### Type parameters

- `TOutput`: Expected domain output type; this assertion does not validate that shape and defaults to unknown.

### Remarks

A proposal never authorizes execution. Domain output validation and action authorization belong to the host.

### Errors and rejections

Error for invalid JSON, envelope or bounded text; structuredClone errors propagate for uncloneable output/arguments.

### Example

```typescript
import { parseWorkflowAgentProposal } from "@alneas/eaos-core/workflow-contracts";
const proposal = parseWorkflowAgentProposal({ schemaVersion: "1.0", summary: "No changes", output: { count: 0 }, evidence: [], actions: [], riskLevel: "low" });
console.log(proposal.summary);
```

<a id="api-PlatformConfig"></a>

## [INTERFACE] `PlatformConfig`

Declarative public origins, ingress, service and authentication settings without credentials.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core/platform/config`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface PlatformConfig {
    appName: string;
    baseDomain: string;
    defaultsVersion?: typeof PLATFORM_DEFAULTS_VERSION;
    environment?: 'production' | 'development';
    networkName?: string;
    origins?: {
        app?: string;
        auth?: string;
    };
    ingress?: {
        appAliases?: string[];
        hostRoutes?: IngressHostRoute[];
        additionalApiPrefixes?: string[];
    };
    services?: {
        backend?: ServiceConfig;
        frontend?: ServiceConfig;
        kratos?: ServiceConfig & {
            adminPort?: number;
        };
    };
    cors?: {
        additionalOrigins?: string[];
        honoAdditionalOrigins?: string[];
        kratosAdditionalOrigins?: string[];
    };
    auth?: {
        uiOrigin?: string;
        defaultBrowserReturnUrl?: string;
        identitySchemas?: IdentitySchemaFile[];
        defaultSchemaId?: string;
        cookie?: {
            name?: string;
            domain?: string;
            path?: string;
            sameSite?: SameSite;
            secure?: boolean;
            persistent?: boolean;
        };
        ui?: Partial<Record<AuthUiFlow, string>>;
        registrationHook?: false | RegistrationHookConfig;
        oidc?: false | {
            google: GoogleOidcConfig;
        };
    };
}
```

### Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `appName` | `string` | Yes | Lowercase DNS label identifying the application and derived network settings. |
| `baseDomain` | `string` | Yes | DNS domain with at least two valid lowercase labels; scopes cookie and managed ingress hosts. |
| `defaultsVersion` | `typeof PLATFORM_DEFAULTS_VERSION` | No | Supported platform defaults version; omission selects PLATFORM_DEFAULTS_VERSION. |
| `environment` | `'production' \| 'development'` | No | Production or development configuration mode; defaults to production with HTTPS/secure-cookie requirements. |
| `networkName` | `string` | No | Host network identity; defaults to appName followed by -network. |
| `origins` | `{     app?: string;     auth?: string; }` | No | Distinct public application and authentication origins; defaults to HTTPS app/auth subdomains of baseDomain. |
| `ingress` | `{     appAliases?: string[];     hostRoutes?: IngressHostRoute[];     additionalApiPrefixes?: string[]; }` | No | Additional exact DNS names for the same app listener/routes; not Docker aliases or CORS grants. |
| `services` | `{     backend?: ServiceConfig;     frontend?: ServiceConfig;     kratos?: ServiceConfig & {         adminPort?: number;     }; }` | No | Optional backend/frontend/Kratos service names and listener/admin port overrides. |
| `cors` | `{     additionalOrigins?: string[];     honoAdditionalOrigins?: string[];     kratosAdditionalOrigins?: string[]; }` | No | Optional extra-origin declarations separated into shared, application-only and Kratos-only grants. |
| `auth` | `{     uiOrigin?: string;     defaultBrowserReturnUrl?: string;     identitySchemas?: IdentitySchemaFile[];     defaultSchemaId?: string;     cookie?: {         name?: string;         domain?: string;         path?: string;         sameSite?: SameSite;         secure?: boolean;         persistent?: boolean;     };     ui?: Partial<Record<AuthUiFlow, string>>;     registrationHook?: false \| RegistrationHookConfig;     oidc?: false \| {         google: GoogleOidcConfig;     }; }` | No | Optional authentication UI, schema, cookie, callback and OIDC settings without runtime credentials. |

### Returns

Type declaration; no runtime value.

### See also

[resolvePlatformConfig](#api-resolvePlatformConfig)

### Public members

#### `appName`

Lowercase DNS label identifying the application and derived network settings.


#### `baseDomain`

DNS domain with at least two valid lowercase labels; scopes cookie and managed ingress hosts.


#### `defaultsVersion`

Supported platform defaults version; omission selects PLATFORM_DEFAULTS_VERSION.


#### `environment`

Production or development configuration mode; defaults to production with HTTPS/secure-cookie requirements.


#### `networkName`

Host network identity; defaults to appName followed by -network.


#### `origins`

Distinct public application and authentication origins; defaults to HTTPS app/auth subdomains of baseDomain.


#### `origins.app`

Optional public application origin; defaults to HTTPS app.<baseDomain>.


#### `origins.auth`

Optional public authentication API origin; defaults to HTTPS auth.<baseDomain> and must differ from app origin.


#### `ingress`

Additional exact DNS names for the same app listener/routes; not Docker aliases or CORS grants.


#### `ingress.appAliases`

Additional exact app DNS names; must stay inside the shared cookie domain and may not claim the auth hostname.


#### `ingress.hostRoutes`

Additional exact DNS-to-upstream routes; conflicting/reserved host claims are rejected.


#### `ingress.additionalApiPrefixes`

Optional additional lowercase absolute API paths without trailing slashes; may not overlap /api or each other.


#### `services`

Optional backend/frontend/Kratos service names and listener/admin port overrides.


#### `services.backend`

Backend service name/port or resolved service; defaults to hono-server on port 3000.


#### `services.frontend`

Frontend service name/port or resolved service; defaults to frontend on port 80.


#### `services.kratos`

Kratos public/admin service configuration or resolved authentication settings.


#### `services.kratos.adminPort`

Kratos administration port; defaults to 4434 and must differ from the public listener port.


#### `cors`

Optional extra-origin declarations separated into shared, application-only and Kratos-only grants.


#### `cors.additionalOrigins`

Extra browser origins shared by Hono and Kratos.


#### `cors.honoAdditionalOrigins`

Extra origins for the application API only; does not expand Kratos access.


#### `cors.kratosAdditionalOrigins`

Extra origins for Kratos only; does not expand application API access.


#### `auth`

Optional authentication UI, schema, cookie, callback and OIDC settings without runtime credentials.


#### `auth.uiOrigin`

External authentication UI; defaults to origins.app and does not add an nginx listener.


#### `auth.defaultBrowserReturnUrl`

Absolute HTTP(S) URL with an optional simple path; defaults to origins.app + '/'.


#### `auth.identitySchemas`

Optional nonempty list of project-relative identity schema files; omission uses builtin default/email-v1.


#### `auth.defaultSchemaId`

Identity-schema ID selected for registration; defaults to the first configured schema or builtin default.


#### `auth.cookie`

Shared auth cookie settings; defaults to secure persistent Lax at root path with a domain covering app/auth/UI/return hosts.


#### `auth.cookie.name`

Auth session cookie name; defaults to ory_kratos_session and special __Host-/__Secure- prefixes have additional constraints.


#### `auth.cookie.domain`

Optional shared cookie DNS domain; defaults to baseDomain and must cover app/auth/UI/return hosts while staying within baseDomain.


#### `auth.cookie.path`

Cookie path; defaults to / and defaults version 1 rejects other values.


#### `auth.cookie.sameSite`

Auth cookie cross-site policy; defaults to Lax. None requires secure true.


#### `auth.cookie.secure`

Auth cookie HTTPS-only flag; defaults to true and is required in production or with SameSite None.


#### `auth.cookie.persistent`

Whether auth cookies persist, or whether a workspace survives execution; cookie default is true and runtime workspace is always false.


#### `auth.ui`

Authentication UI flow paths or derived absolute URLs; no UI routes are deployed by resolution.


#### `auth.registrationHook`

Internal callback only; the host must supply hook authentication and business handling.


#### `auth.oidc`

Explicit opt-in; client ID and secret are host runtime bindings, never config values.


#### `auth.oidc.google`

Explicit Google OIDC provider configuration; credentials are separate host runtime bindings.



### Example

See the owning declaration and linked feature guide for usage; no standalone example is documented in source.

Imports: `@alneas/eaos-core`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/index`, `@alneas/eaos-core/plugin-sdk/define-plugin`.

### Signature

```typescript
interface PluginContext<TServices = Record<string, unknown>> {
    readonly pluginId: string;
    readonly principal: Readonly<PlatformPrincipal> & {
        readonly entitlements: TenantEntitlements | null;
    };
```
